newsitem.title: MEXICO: Red alert as Mexico City volcano bellows ash.
newsitem.headline: Red alert as Mexico City volcano bellows ash.

text.p: Mexican emergency officials put the huge Popocatepetl volcano southeast of Mexico City on red alert on Monday after it spewed out a giant cloud of ash, news reports said.

The red alert is the highest warning signal for volcanoes in Mexico and authorities said they were discussing whether to evacuate thousands of residents in nearby towns, the reports on television and radio said.

Roberto Meli, an Interior Ministry official responsible for disaster prevention, told Mexico's main television broadcaster Televisa the red alert was triggered by unusually strong seismic activity and that the crater belched out ash and burning rocks. But he said Popocatepetl had calmed down since the worst of the emissions.
He said no evacuation orders had yet been given to the tens of thousands of people who live near its southeastern flanks, but that emergency vehicles were moving in just in case.

The volcano has blown out ash and steam on numerous occasions this year, and has been volatile since December 1994 -- the last time Mexicans were evacuated from nearby areas. Meli said the earth tremors that triggered Monday's instability were worse than in December 1994.
National network Radio Red said ash was expected to rain down on southern suburbs of Mexico City, which has some 18 million inhabitants and lies in the volcano's shadow.
